what: MARGINED_MS_BACKFILL_SELECT_SWEEP across the full admissible GHOSTREPLAY_ACCURACY_BACKFILL_BATCH domain (1..MAX_BATCH_SIZE).
why: The frozen scalar prices a statement whose cost depends on the operator-chosen batch size. Evidence for g-b-sweep-batch-cost.
naming_note: `what` names MARGINED_MS_BACKFILL_SELECT_SWEEP because that is the constant this domain was measured against. g-b-sweep-batch-cost deleted it: the sweep is now MARGINED_MS_BACKFILL_SWEEP_SCAN (ms, relation) + MARGINED_US_BACKFILL_SWEEP_PER_PAGE (us, per page), fitted from these points. The old name is kept here for the same reason `fits.withdrawn` is: this file is the record of how the model was arrived at.
database: gr_p1_sweep -- disposable restore of ghostreplay-20260724T101501Z.dump with populations synthesized
statement: keyset SELECT_BATCH_* page: WHERE <population predicate> AND id > :last ORDER BY id LIMIT :n, swept to exhaustion; one 'sweep' = every page of one pass, so pages = ceil(N_stale / batch_size) + 1
sessions_synthesized_note: This copy was never row-cloned: its 4,184 game_sessions rows are the restore's own. The flag exists so a copy grown by --synthesize-sessions, whose clones carry no session_moves rows, can only ever be offered as kind: 'sweep_domain'.

dimensions_before.note: These are POST-synthesis dimensions -- what the timed statements actually saw. Each timing must stay paired with them; substituting pre-synthesis dimensions without rebasing the timings is mismatched provenance.
dimensions_before.sibling_copies_note: The seven sizing copies share a source restore and a game_sessions row count (4,184) but are NOT identical data: gr_p1_atomic and gr_p1_b100/250/500/1000 ran stale+repair synthesis (130,676 moves, N_stale=646), gr_p1_sweep ran stale only (131,676 moves, N_stale=1,646), gr_p1_empty ran stamped (131,676 moves, N_stale=0). Their game_sessions relations read 5,414,912..6,848,512 bytes -- PARTLY dead tuples from rewrite and vacuum state, PARTLY a genuinely different post-synthesis relation. A timing may only be normalized by the basis of the copy it actually ran on.

frozen_basis.note: max(6000/4184, 10010624/5414912) = 1.84871; the byte ratio wins. Sibling copies carrying the SAME 4184 game_sessions rows read 5414912..6848512 bytes -- PARTLY dead tuples from synthesis rewrite and vacuum state, PARTLY a genuinely different post-synthesis relation, since the copies ran different syntheses (see dimensions_of_this_copy.sibling_copies_note). The factor is therefore only valid for timings taken on THIS copy.

runs.note: Original domain run. Per-trial timings were NOT kept -- this is why run C exists. Maxima only; do not refit from these. The 4-page point (13.60 ms against a 4.60 ms median) is a host outlier.

Re-measurement with every trial preserved. ELEVEN of the twelve maxima exceed run B's at the same page count -- the tendency of a larger sample, not a guarantee: a maximum over more independent trials has a higher EXPECTED value, but monotonicity holds only for a cumulative maximum over appended trials, and these are two independent runs. The twelfth FELL (4 pages, 13.60 -> 4.94) because that is where run B's outlier had landed. The outlier itself moved from 4 pages to 3, confirming host noise rather than a page-count property. A 3-trial maximum is an estimate of a bound, not a bound.

published_rounded_up.note: Both coefficients rounded UP. The construction makes the line TOUCH its worst point (pages=824), so nearest-rounding either coefficient for display pushes it below that point: 14.5556 + 0.170443*824 = 155.000632 vs a measured 155.0007. A bound's coefficients round one way only.

fits.envelope_construction: OLS intercept shifted up by the maximum positive residual, so envelope(pages_i) >= max_i by construction.
fits.invariant: for every measured point i: envelope(pages_i) >= max_i, and therefore ceil(3*envelope(pages_i)) >= ceil(3*max_i). NOTE the earlier value of this flag was false, produced by comparing a real 3*envelope against an integer ceil(3*max) -- an off-by-rounding in the CHECK, not in the envelope. Compare ceil to ceil. A frozen model must keep passing this or it has stopped being conservative.

withdrawn.why: OLS through a set of maxima is a central tendency, not a bound: at 824 pages it predicts 131.20 vs a measured 134.66, and 3x the coefficients (393.59) is still under ceil(3*134.66) = 404. It was also unreproducible -- computed over 12 maxima, published beside an 8-row table, and copied into the bead as 11 rows, which refit to 3.029 + 0.15517.
